attributes.law_screen: claim.law.webfrank-pinned-function-source-freeze.20260831.v1 SCREENED FIRST and it is the reason this function was workable at all: config/GUNE5D/webfrank.json pins PointLineDist2D in game/world/btricol, so that sibling is SOURCE-FROZEN, but LineLineDist and BTriLineCol carry no rule and were free to edit. claim.law.declaration-initializer-split-controls-entry-schedule.20260830.v1 APPLIED as the basis for AXIS2 (scalar decl reordering to move web-creation order) - measured byte-neutral, so the law's entry-schedule effect does NOT extend to register-resident f32 scalars in this function. claim.law.independent-statement-reorder-matches-target-schedule.20260830.v1 SCREENED and deliberately NOT used: the target's evaluation order is already cy, cx, cz exactly as written (verified instruction-by-instruction from the fmsubs operands), so reordering the three statements would move AWAY from the target. claim.law.chained-init-constant-share.20260829.v1 n/a (no shared FP literal at entry; the only pool read is the lbl_80345D50 comparison operand, already position-matched). claim.law.repeated-fp-pool-literal-first-load-is-position-invariant.20260831.v1 SCREENED n/a for the same reason. claim.law.reload-vs-cache-liveness.20260829.v1 and claim.law.store-placement-family.20260829.v1 SCREENED n/a: the opcode multiset is IDENTICAL 464/464, so the load/reload COUNT is already exactly right and no caching change can be neutral. claim.law.narrow-local-reextend-on-read.20260830.v1 n/a (all-float function).
attributes.residual: REGISTER_ONLY/SCHEDULE, real 272, 464/464 instructions, opcode multiset IDENTICAL (fndiff --ops classifies it 'pure reorder, schedule-class'). Semantics are already exact: the three cross products were verified against the target's fmsubs operand pairs and compute cy = dirB->z*dirA->x - dirB->x*dirA->z, cx = dirB->y*dirA->z - dirB->z*dirA->y, cz = dirB->x*dirA->y - dirB->y*dirA->x, evaluated in that order, matching the target exactly. The entire residual is seeded by ONE permutation at the top of the function body: the first four loads are target [dirA->z 8(r7), dirB->x 0(r4), dirB->z 8(r4), dirA->y 4(r7)] but ours [dirB->x, dirA->z, dirB->z, dirA->y] - only the FIRST PAIR is swapped, the second pair agrees. Every later difference is the FPR renaming that follows: target homes dirA->y/dirA->x/pointA.x/pointA.y/pointA.z/pointB.y/pointB.z/denom in f27/f31/f30/f26/f25/f29/f24/f28, ours in f12/f29/f31/f13/f26/f30/f25/f24; both save exactly f24-f31 via _savefpr_24 and both use the same eight nonvolatiles, so this is a pure re-mapping over an identical register budget, not a pressure difference. AXES TRIED, all three byte-NEUTRAL (real stayed exactly 272, multiset stayed IDENTICAL): AXIS1 reverse the subtrahend's operands (`dirA->z * dirB->x`); AXIS2 reorder the cx/cy/cz declarations to match assignment order (cy first); AXIS3 orient ALL three cross products dirA-first (`dirA->x*dirB->z - dirA->z*dirB->x` etc). The three neutrals together establish that MWCC canonicalizes commutative FP multiply operand order in the front end, so the source CANNOT express which operand of a product is loaded first, and that register-resident f32 scalar declaration order does not drive FPR web creation order. WEBFRANK-READY, and an unusually clean instance: the residual decomposes into exactly one adjacent-independent-load transposition (two lfs with different base registers and no aliasing between them, so the permutation dependence audit is trivial) plus a bijective FPR renaming over a fixed eight-register nonvolatile set with identical opcodes at identical positions - precisely the form the hardened guards (form-aware masks + renaming bisimulation + permutation dependence audit) are built to prove. Worth 272 real lines and would take btricol's LineLineDist from fuzzy 97.06% to exact. No rule authored here per lane instructions.
